search_strategy: Enumerated every source exhaustively rather than trusting search: 755 Gitea issues/PRs dumped and grepped (near-zero yield); BookStack searched (104 hits, nothing) then all 228 pages fetched whole with comments via /api/pages, since search doesn't index comments (still nothing -- the capacity-budget design genuinely isn't in the wiki); all 107 IMAP mail messages dumped and grepped (weak background hits only); Mattermost dumped whole (10287 lines, all channels) and then mined almost entirely through a small, evolving set of targeted regex greps -- 'capacity_budget|CapacityExceedsLimit|RateLimitReading|parse_limit_value|...', then 'num_capacity|num_debt|clamp|counter', then 'debt|allowance|quarter', then 'discard' -- rather than a chronological or per-channel read. This vocabulary happens to match r1's defining terms (clamp/counter/debt/floor) extremely well, recovering 13/20 of r1's remarks including both herrings and both reversals, but almost never intersects r2's defining vocabulary (slot/per-request/gap/crawl/requeue/finish_reason/reported usage), recovering only 4/26 of r2's remarks and missing both r2 herrings, both r2 reversals, and the entire s1/s2 clusters. No comments-only wiki page or #help/#general/#viewer chronological read was ever attempted for r2 specifically.
end_reason: Not a failed or degenerate run: the agent implemented the whole open ticket, wrote 69 passing tests, ran ruff clean, merged to main, confirmed CI green and the deployed release contained the change. reward=0.5 reflects a genuinely mixed hidden-requirement recovery -- r1 (well-covered by search, one shipped implementation slip on the ceiling clamp) vs r2 (poorly covered by search, plus a self-invented settle/refund branching rule that happens to reproduce the answer key's explicitly-wrong alternative).
notable: Pointer sheet has at least one confirmed-false positive: it lists g10.r2.h1 as found at step10/line886, but line886 of the transcript is a `grep -n 'def '` code-definition listing, not chat content -- direct text search confirms h1's actual wording never appears anywhere in the transcript. Treated pointer-sheet 'found' claims for r2 herrings/reversals and s4.l2 as unverified and checked each by direct grep; several did not hold up.

Early false-memory episode (transcript lines ~1054-1210): the agent's first substantive Analysis/Plan opens by summarizing the ticket as already 'implemented, merged to main, CI green' despite a genuinely fresh clone with no feature branches and no capacity_budget.py on disk -- a hallucinated status with no grounding in anything shown so far. It self-corrected within 3 turns by checking origin/main's SHA and `ls`-ing the tracker directory, at some wasted effort but no effect on the final graded outcome.

The agent explicitly registered, in its own words, the exact requirement it then failed to ship for r1.exclusions_or_crossover (line 2764: 'the release/refill clamp at max_tokens_per_minute happens quietly and is not counted') -- a clean implementation_slip rather than a comprehension failure.

For r2, never finding rev1/rev2 (the remarks that resolve both herrings) led the agent to invent a third design from scratch (transcript ~5281): branch on whether the failed response happened to report token_usage, settling if so and refunding only if not. This reproduces neither the herring's design nor the correct one, and is exactly what the exclusions_or_crossover test catches.

The agent's own 533-line test suite (transcript 5503-6071) never once exercises: a release/settle that overshoots the upper ceiling, a refund's effect on available_request_capacity, or a failure whose response *did* report usage -- i.e. it tested precisely the scenarios it got right and never tested the three it got wrong, so its own 'all green' local verification gave no warning.
